_comment: BASE-OWNED template approvals for check_security_gate.py (decision 2 of the 2026-10-21 publish plan). An approval turns a P1 finding in printing-press generated code into a reviewed one ONLY when the gate establishes mechanically that the flagged code is the reviewed template: same tool, rule, file and enclosing declaration; every declaration in 'slice' byte-identical with identical resolved references (go/types, via tools/maintainer/declgraph) on the scanner's build target; the slice closed except for the declarations named in 'exclude'; no declaration outside the slice using a guarded slice member except the 'entries'; no replace, go.work or vendor; the same go language version, godebug settings, press version and reviewed module hashes. Anything not established stays a P1 and the ordinary suppression PR to security_suppressions.json applies. The gate reads this file from the trusted base ref, never from the PR. Record a new approval with --emit-approval from a REVIEWED tree, and land it as its own reviewed PR. Every 'exclude' and 'entries' reason and every precondition is the human review; the hashes only bind it to the code that was read.

exclude.func {MOD}/internal/store.DecodeJSONObje: Called on a row's stored JSON after the batch query executed; its result only sets row.storageID and cannot change the query text.
exclude.func {MOD}/internal/store.applyParentKey: Runs after the batch query with parameterized statements on a copy of one row; cannot alter bareWhere, an immutable string local to migrateParentKeyStorageIDs.
exclude.func {MOD}/internal/store.ensureParentKe: Receives bareWhere by value and returns only an error, so it cannot alter the string later passed to loadParentKeyLegacyBatch. Its own SQL is not this finding.
exclude.func {MOD}/internal/store.parentKeyBareI: Receives bareWhere by value and returns only a bool and an error, so it cannot alter the string later passed to loadParentKeyLegacyBatch. Its own SQL is not this finding.
exclude.func {MOD}/internal/store.resourceStorag: Called after the batch query executed; its result only sets row.storageID and cannot change the query text.
exclude.func {MOD}/internal/store.tableExists: Returns a bool for a fixed table name; it never sees bareWhere.
exclude.type {MOD}/internal/store.Store: Receiver of migrateParentKeyStorageIDs, which never reads it; Store's methods are connector code outside this finding.
exclude.var {MOD}/internal/store.resourceParentK: Spec-derived per connector. Its keys reach SQL text only through parentKeyLegacyBareWhere, whose quote-doubling makes any key a string literal; loadParentKeyLegacyBatch reads it again only after the query ran, to decide whether to re-key a row.

entries.func {MOD}/internal/store.parentKeyLegac: A pure function of its argument; calling it elsewhere cannot change what migrateParentKeyStorageIDs computes.
entries.method {MOD}/internal/store.Store.migrat: Neither its receiver nor its parameters (ctx, conn) reach the query text: it computes bareWhere itself from the resource type list. Store.migrate calls it on every open.

preconditions: The flagged statement builds `SELECT id, resource_type, data FROM resources WHERE ` + bareWhere and then appends only string literals; afterType, afterID and the batch size are bound as ? arguments.

bareWhere reaches loadParentKeyLegacyBatch only from migrateParentKeyStorageIDs (enforced: no other declaration may call it), which computes it as parentKeyLegacyBareWhere(sorted keys of resourceParentKeyColumns) and passes it on unchanged.

parentKeyLegacyBareWhere wraps each resource type in single quotes and doubles every embedded quote, which is the complete escaping rule for an SQLite string literal (SQLite has no backslash escapes), so the predicate is a literal IN list whatever the keys contain. That is why the spec-derived map may differ per connector.

Checked by script: those three functions, the row type and the batch-size constant are byte-identical to the template with identical resolved references on every release target; nothing outside them calls loadParentKeyLegacyBatch; no replace, go.work or vendor; same go language version, godebug settings and press version.

preconditions: httpTokenEnvVar is the NAME of the environment variable the MCP server's HTTP transport reads its bearer token from at runtime (<ENV PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN), not a credential. gosec G101 matches the identifier's 'Token' substring.

Checked by script: the constant's type and exact value equal the template's after the connector-name substitution, so the value is exactly the connector's own <ENV PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN and nothing else. A constant has no inputs, so no other code can feed it.

exclude.func {MOD}/internal/cli.legacyStoreAdopt: Builds the list of file paths claimClosedStore opens with os.Open; a path never reaches an unsafe.Pointer, a buffer length or an integer conversion.

entries.func {MOD}/internal/cli.claimClosedStore: Its only parameter is a path string used to os.Open the store files; the memory safety of the proc_info calls does not depend on it. adoptLegacyScopedStoreLocked calls it.

preconditions: store_adopt_darwin.go builds only for darwin/amd64 and darwin/arm64. Before renaming a legacy credential-scoped store it asks the kernel through proc_info (unix.Syscall6) whether another process holds the store files open.

unsafe is used only in darwinPIDs, darwinFDs, darwinVnodeID and darwinProcInfo, to hand a Go-allocated buffer and a length derived from unsafe.Sizeof to the kernel to fill: no pointer arithmetic, no conversion of foreign memory, buffer growth bounded (n < 1<<20).

darwinProcInfo, the only function that takes a raw pointer and a length, may be called only from the reviewed file (enforced). The one outside entry, claimClosedStore, takes a path string that reaches only os.Open and Fstat.
golang.org/x/sys (Syscall6, SYS_PROC_INFO, Fstat, Stat_t) is the reviewed version with the reviewed go.sum hashes.
Checked by script: the whole file, each declaration in it and its imports are byte-identical with identical resolved references on both darwin targets.

entries.func {MOD}/internal/cli.darwinStoreFileU: Called by claimClosedStore with an open *os.File; every converted value comes from Fstat or proc_info, not from the caller.

preconditions: Reported only by a darwin gosec run (local macOS checks). The flagged conversions widen or reinterpret values the kernel returned: int(pid) and uint64(fd) for process and descriptor numbers proc_info listed, and uint32(self.Dev) to compare Fstat's signed 32-bit dev_t bits with proc_info's unsigned st_dev.
None of them sizes an allocation or indexes a slice; a wrapped value can only make a kernel call fail, which declines the rename.

Checked by script: both functions and everything they call (darwinPIDs, darwinFDs, darwinProcInfo and the proc_info struct types) are byte-identical with identical resolved references on both darwin targets, with the reviewed golang.org/x/sys.
